title: Energy Transfer Just Raised Its 2026 Guidance. Is the Stock Still a Buy?
author: James Halley
description: Energy Transfer raised its 2026 EBITDA guidance by $500 million to $18.8-19.1 billion following strong Q2 results, with distributable cash flow up 32% year-over-year. The company continues expanding infrastructure for AI data centers and natural gas exports, raised its dividend for the 19th consecutive quarter, and trades at a modest 9.7x EV/EBITDA multiple. However, a 29% decline in natural gas prices since January poses a risk to volume growth if sustained.

title: Bloom Energy Stock Has Surged 150% in 2026. Is It Still a Buy?
author: Steven Porrello
description: Bloom Energy has rebounded sharply in August after a brutal July decline, with shares up 150% year-to-date. The fuel-cell provider's 'time-to-power' advantage is driving explosive sales growth from AI data centers, with Q2 revenue crossing $1 billion for the first time and 2026 guidance of $3.9-4.2 billion. However, the stock trades at a lofty 81x forward earnings, and manufacturing constraints may limit growth. The author maintains a bullish long-term outlook despite near-term volatility risks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth (tripled product revenue last quarter, $1B+ Q2 revenue), explosive sales trajectory with 2026 guidance of $3.9-4.2B (roughly double YoY), and significant competitive advantage in 'time-to-power' for data center deployments. Author recommends as a buy for long-term investors despite acknowledging high valuation and volatility risks.

title: Alphabet vs. Oracle: Which Is the Better AI Stock to Own for the Next 5 Years?
author: Jennifer Saibil
description: Alphabet and Oracle are the third and fourth-largest cloud infrastructure companies globally, both benefiting from AI tailwinds. Alphabet leads with its Gemini LLM and integrated ecosystem across Search, Android, and YouTube, showing strong revenue growth (24% YoY) and positive cash flow. Oracle is building data centers and raising capital ($45-50B in fiscal 2026) to compete, with impressive RPO growth of 363% YoY. The analyst recommends Alphabet as the better 5-year investment due to its cash-positive position, diversified business portfolio, and proven AI monetization capabilities.

title: If You'd Invested $10,000 in Oracle a Year Ago, Here's What It Would Be Worth Today
author: Daniel Sparks
description: A $10,000 investment in Oracle made one year ago would be worth approximately $6,300 today. Despite strong AI-driven demand with remaining performance obligations reaching $638 billion and cloud infrastructure revenue accelerating to $18.1 billion, the stock declined 38% due to massive capital expenditures ($55.7 billion in fiscal 2026) resulting in negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion, significant workforce reductions of 21,000 employees, and substantial shareholder dilution through debt and equity raises. The market repriced Oracle from a high-growth software company to a capital-intensive AI infrastructure builder.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Oracle demonstrated strong AI-driven demand growth with RPO reaching $638 billion and cloud infrastructure revenue accelerating to 93% YoY growth, the stock declined 38% over the year due to unsustainable capital expenditure levels ($55.7 billion, more than doubling YoY), negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion, significant workforce reductions (21,000 employees), and substantial shareholder dilution through $43 billion in debt and $5 billion in equity raises plus planned $40 billion more in fiscal 2027. The market repriced the company from a premium software valuation to a capital-intensive infrastructure builder, reflecting concerns about the sustainability of growth at this cost.

title: Bloom Energy vs. Oklo: Which AI-Power Stock Is the Smarter Buy Now?
author: Leo Sun
description: Bloom Energy and Oklo both target AI-driven energy demand through different technologies—Bloom with solid oxide fuel cells and Oklo with microreactors. Bloom has surged 2,030% over two years with established revenue and major customers, while Oklo has gained 510% but remains pre-revenue and speculative. Despite Bloom's strong valuation multiples, it remains the better buy compared to Oklo's overvalued 156x 2028 sales multiple.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Established revenue of billions, serves major customers (Oracle, CoreWeave, Equinix), strong growth projections (70% revenue CAGR, 120% EBITDA CAGR through 2028), reasonable valuation multiples (7x 2028 sales), and backed by Brookfield Asset Management. Analyst recommendation favors it as the smarter buy.

Pre-revenue with no deployed microreactors yet, expected deployment in 2027-2028, projected 2028 revenue of only $55M, extremely overvalued at 156x 2028 sales, negative adjusted EBITDA, and characterized as speculative. Too much optimism already priced into the stock.
